questions.stem: In the formula distance = (speed x time) / 2, why do we divide by 2 when calculating depth using ultrasound?

options.text: Because ultrasound travels at half the speed of sound
Because the ultrasound pulse travels to the boundary and back, so the total distance is twice the depth
Because only half the ultrasound is reflected
Because the frequency is halved during reflection

questions.explanation: We divide by 2 because the ultrasound pulse makes a round trip: it travels from the transducer to the reflecting boundary and then back to the transducer. The total distance measured is therefore twice the actual depth of the boundary.
